clue.text: Bad accidents causing water loss

definitions.note: used as an adjective: a drying agent is one that causes moisture loss

indicators.note: bad here signals that the letters of the next word are spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Bad accidents leave people dehydrated.
explanation.definitionFit: A desiccant is a drying agent, something that draws moisture out of whatever is around it.

clue.text: Northerner brings up boy given silly names

indicators.note: in a down clue brings up means the word is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: silly signals that the letters of the next word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A northern man raises his son but gives him daft names.
explanation.definitionFit: A dalesman is a man from the Yorkshire Dales, so a northerner in England.

clue.text: Lots of fish in shallow water

definitions.meaning: a large group of fish swimming together
a sandbank or place where the water is not deep

explanation.definitionFit: A shoal is both a large school of fish and a shallow stretch of sea.

clue.text: Jane's sister was unbelievable

parts.note: Jane Austen's sister bore the name of the Trojan prophetess cursed never to be believed

explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen's sister shared the name of the Trojan seer whose true prophecies nobody believed.

clue.text: Won't one enlighten Protestants?

parts.note: a Roman Catholic lamp would hardly enlighten Protestants

explanation.definitionFit: An arc lamp gives light from an electric arc; read as a Roman Catholic lamp it suits no Protestant.

clue.text: Houses joined in contest after school period, losing marks

indicators.note: after says the contest comes behind the school-period piece
losing says a letter is taken away from the term

parts.note: a term is a period of the school year
M is an abbreviation for mark, the old German currency
a race is a contest

explanation.surface: Schools hold a house competition after term, with points deducted.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is a row of houses joined together, a common British housing style.

clue.text: In greasy spoon, hot fodder

indicators.note: In at the front says the hot piece is placed within the cafe word

parts.note: a greasy spoon is a cheap cafe, in British slang a caff
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone in a cheap cafe is served hot animal feed.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'greasy spoon' is British slang for a cheap, basic cafe, also called a caff.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaff is chopped straw or husks fed to livestock, a kind of fodder.

clue.text: Trainee needs time in Paris to secure lady's heart

indicators.note: to secure says the time zone holds the next piece within it

parts.note: CET, Central European Time, is the time zone used in Paris

indicators.note: heart picks the middle letters of lady

explanation.surface: A trainee needs time in Paris to win a woman's affection.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a trainee in the armed forces or police.

clue.text: Dance band, losing leader, named replacement

indicators.note: losing leader means the word drops its opening letter

parts.note: the Halle is a Manchester orchestra, so a band

indicators.note: replacement signals that the letters of named are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A dance band loses its leader and names a substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hallé is a famous Manchester orchestra; without its H it gives ALLE, and MANDE comes from rearranging named.
explanation.definitionFit: An allemande is a stately Renaissance and Baroque dance of German origin.

clue.text: Looks through paper, most visionary

indicators.note: through says the looks run through the inside of the newspaper

parts.note: the FT, the Financial Times, is a newspaper
looks here are eyes, as in giving someone the eye

explanation.surface: Someone peers through the newspaper, being most far-sighted.
explanation.definitionFit: Fey can mean clairvoyant, able to foresee the future, so the superlative means most visionary.

clue.text: Asian country containing one county

indicators.note: containing says the Asian country holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: Laos is a country in South-East Asia
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An Asian nation encloses a single county within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Laois is a county in the Irish province of Leinster.

clue.text: Pretty girl in old hat a model — that's the last straw

definitions.text: a model — that's the last straw

indicators.note: in says the girl is set inside the old-hat word

parts.note: old hat means stale and trite, that is corny
a doll is slang for a pretty girl

explanation.surface: A pretty girl in an unfashionable hat models, and someone has had enough.
explanation.definitionFit: A corn dolly is a figure plaited from straw, traditionally from the last sheaf of the harvest.

clue.text: Consult an authority, bottling fruit

indicators.note: bottling says the answer is kept inside the words, as liquid inside a bottle

explanation.surface: Ask an expert about preserving fruit in jars.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultana is a dried seedless grape, a type of fruit.

clue.text: Olympian figure calls painting a failure

indicators.note: calls signals that the phrase is spoken and its sound gives the entry

parts.note: painting is art, and a failure is a miss: art a miss

explanation.surface: A god on Olympus declares a picture unsuccessful.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemis, goddess of the hunt, was one of the twelve Olympian deities of Greek myth.

clue.text: Weight-lifting drug?

parts.note: read not as a steroid for gym lifters but as a medicine that lifts a weight off the mind

explanation.definitionFit: Such medicines treat low mood, lifting the heavy weight of depression from a patient.

clue.text: Ordered to keep her strangely quiet: that's the limit

indicators.note: to keep says the ordered word holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: told means ordered, as in told to do something

indicators.note: strangely signals the letters of her are mixed up

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: Told to keep her oddly silent, someone says enough is enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' reads as an adjective describing her, but it is the verb told; 'strangely' scrambles her before 'to keep' encloses it with the call for quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A threshold is a boundary point or limit at which something begins or ends.

clue.text: Like some wings, cleaned towards the rear

parts.note: swept means cleaned with a broom
back means towards the rear

explanation.surface: Someone cleaned towards the back of the room.
explanation.definitionFit: Swept-back wings are angled rearwards, as on jet aircraft.

clue.text: Having panned meal, one abstaining — nothing to fight about

parts.note: O, the round figure, stands for nothing

indicators.note: about says the fight goes round the abstainer

parts.note: a melee is a confused fight
TT means teetotal, one who abstains from alcohol

explanation.surface: After a criticised meal, a teetotaller sees no reason to argue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panned' looks like criticised, but here means cooked in a pan.
explanation.definitionFit: An omelette is beaten egg cooked in a frying pan, a meal made in a pan.

clue.text: Not skinny, and smiling hugely?

parts.note: the idiom means wide in the hips; read literally it is wide in the beam, a beam being a broad smile

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone wide around the hips, not slender at all.

clue.text: God we omitted from US motto, for safety

indicators.note: omitted from says the named words are cut out of the motto

parts.note: In God We Trust is the official motto of the United States
these words are removed as written

explanation.surface: God and we are dropped from America's motto for safety's sake.
explanation.definitionFit: Property held in trust is kept safe by another on someone's behalf.

clue.text: Silk had meal, fine and rich, sent up

indicators.note: in a down clue sent up means the pieces are written upwards, reversed

parts.note: ate means had a meal
F is short for fine, as on pencils
fat means rich, as in fatty food

explanation.surface: A silk-clad diner ate a fine rich meal and was mocked for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The one indicator 'sent up' turns the whole run ATEFFAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp, lustrous fabric traditionally woven from silk.

clue.text: Slopping drink across cheek is a mistake

indicators.note: across says the drink stretches over the cheek, round it

parts.note: to sup is to drink by sips, often noisily and sloppily
lip means cheek, impudence

explanation.surface: Spilling a drink over someone's insolence is an error.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip-up is an informal word for a minor error or blunder.

clue.text: Survive — to turn off the lights?

definitions.meaning: to endure longer than something, to keep going to the end
the person who is final to leave a room is the one expected to switch off the lights

explanation.definitionFit: To last out is to survive to the end; the final one to go is expected to turn off the lights.

clue.text: Address to Margaret a letter

parts.note: O is the vocative address, as in O Lord
Meg is a pet form of Margaret

explanation.surface: Someone writes a letter addressed to Margaret.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Disastrous, lots being affected

definitions.meaning: a lot is one's destiny, so something that affects lots is full of destiny

explanation.definitionFit: Fateful events are momentous, often ruinous, and decide people's destinies or lots.

clue.text: Conspicuously display emblem on uniform

definitions.meaning: a coloured patch worn on a military uniform to show the unit

explanation.definitionFit: To flash is to show off; a flash is a military badge sewn on a uniform sleeve.

clue.text: Carry out assessment of twee novelist

definitions.meaning: to pursue or carry through a task to its end
a critic's verdict on a twee writer's style: the prose is cute

explanation.definitionFit: To prosecute a plan or war is to carry it through; split, it reads prose cute.

clue.text: Stop aboard a container ship, detained initially

indicators.note: detained says the container holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: a vat is a large container for liquids

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of ship

explanation.surface: A container ship is held at port and must halt.
explanation.definitionFit: Avast is a nautical command meaning stop, used on board ship.

clue.text: City father has short double

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: dual means double, twofold

explanation.surface: A city's founding father has a short twin.
explanation.definitionFit: Padua is a city in north-eastern Italy, near Venice.

clue.text: Cooked shortcake assumed to go fast

definitions.note: a phrase describing a noun: footwear put on so one can run fast

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are fiddled with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A baked biscuit is gobbled up quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assumed' means put on, as clothing is: the definition describes footwear donned for speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Track shoes are spiked running shoes worn by athletes so they can sprint faster.
